title: COFF — Common Object File Format
description: The container a compiler hands the linker: a 20-byte header that says this is an object and not an image, 40-byte section headers where every address is zero, and the symbol and relocation tables that let the linker place code whose final address nobody knows yet. Every byte verified against real objects produced by clang for three targets (x64 MSVC, x64 GNU, i386 MSVC) and cross-checked by two independently written parsers.
author: Underlayer
completion_criteria: Decode a COFF object file end to end, resolve every name through the string table, and explain what a relocation asks the linker to do.

concepts.title: Why COFF Exists
concepts.description: The link step, what relocatable means, and why a COFF object cannot be executed.

concepts.title: The File Header
concepts.description: All seven fields of IMAGE_FILE_HEADER, and how Machine tells you the pointer width.

concepts.title: The Section Header
concepts.description: Ten fields in forty bytes, and the section that reserves four bytes it does not contain.

concepts.title: Section Characteristics
concepts.description: The flags the linker obeys, and why alignment is a four-bit field that seven bitmask tests get wrong at once.

concepts.title: The String Table
concepts.description: The pool every long name resolves through, and the three different encodings that can point into it.

concepts.title: The Symbol Table
concepts.description: The 18-byte symbol, storage classes, and an aux record whose field order is not the documented one.

concepts.title: Relocations
concepts.description: Ten bytes per unanswered question, the AMD64 type table, and the packed layout the compiler does not emit.

concepts.title: COMDAT and Duplicate Sections
concepts.description: How a linker is told which of two identical sections to keep, why the checksum can differ, and how the dialects differ.

concepts.title: bigobj
concepts.description: The over-65,535 variant whose header relocates its fields rather than widening them, and the 0x0000FFFF signature it shares with short-import libraries.

concepts.title: The .lib Archive
concepts.description: The ar container a .lib is: the 8-byte magic, the 60-byte member header with its decimal size field, and the two symbol indexes that use different byte orders.

concepts.title: Line Numbers
concepts.description: The two section-header fields that are always zero, the 6-byte record layout verified by construction, and why the values mean nothing before the link.

concepts.title: The Link
concepts.description: A real COFF-to-PE link, watched step by step: sections given addresses, four zero bytes becoming a displacement, and sections dropped by flags read out of the header.

concepts.title: Map Files
concepts.description: The linker's plain-text transcript: the discard list, the memory configuration, the linker-defined symbols, and the *fill* rows that account for 15 of 69 bytes of .text.

concepts.title: COMDAT in the Linker
concepts.description: COMDAT deduplication observed working end to end, and a reproduced silent miscompilation: two different function bodies, one checksum, and a linker that discarded the wrong one.

concepts.title: ARM64 Relocations
concepts.description: A real ARM64 object: five relocation types from four functions, the two-instruction pairs that only make sense together, and a 26-bit branch field that must be range-checked.

concepts.title: Thread Local Storage
concepts.description: The .tls$ section: characteristics byte-identical to .data, contents that are a template rather than the variables, and a link that cannot be completed on this machine.

concepts.title: Weak Externals
concepts.description: A third symbol state: storage class 105, the auxiliary record that names a fallback, and a branch in the generated code as the observable cost.

concepts.title: Linker Directives in a Section
concepts.description: A section whose contents are instructions to the linker: 23 bytes decoded, and observed being discarded with a controlled comparison as the control.
